EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by aliphatic C–H features (2955, 2862; GFQ-003) and a strong CH2 scissoring band at 1446 cm⁻¹, consistent with a saturated backbone. The weak, single band at 3317 cm⁻¹ fits a secondary N–H/O–H stretch (GFQ-001, GFQ-002), favoring a molecule with one N–H and one O–H rather than multiple donors. The medium bands at 863 and 1036 cm⁻¹ are characteristic of cyclic ether ring modes (C–O–C ring breathing/stretch) expected for a morpholine ring, and the 1134–1209 cm⁻¹ region suits C–O/C–N stretches in such heterocycles. OCC[C@H]1COCCN1 (a morpholine with a hydroxyethyl side chain) matches this pattern better than candidates lacking a ring ether or having no N–H.
